The ARD spec

Source: vignettes/articles/ard-spec.Rmd
ard-spec.Rmd

The ARD spec is the study’s analyses as a workbook. tfl_ard_code() writes the R program it stands for – cards / cardx calls, one per analysis row – and tfl_build_ard() runs that program and saves one study ARD (analysis results data) that every table then reads.

The program is meant to be read. A dataset is read in one line, an analysis set is one subset(), an analysis data is one pipe, an analysis is one call. It is written the way a programmer would write it, so that it can be reviewed, copied into a study and finished by hand when needed.

library(tflspec)

study <- file.path(tempdir(), "ard-study")
dir.create(file.path(study, "data"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(adsl, file.path(study, "data", "adsl.rds"))   # the sample study's ADaM
saveRDS(adae, file.path(study, "data", "adae.rds"))

df <- function(...) data.frame(..., stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

The sheets

Sheet One row per Holds
study key id (the subject key), output (where the ARD goes), source (R files of the study’s own functions)
datasets dataset dataset, level, path (relative to the study folder), derive (columns made on reading)
populations analysis set population_id, dataset, where, derive
analysis_data named data of a report output_id, data_id, label, from, population_id, subjects, where, add, derive, keep, distinct, code
analyses analysis output_id, analysis_id, method, data or dataset + population_id, where, by, strata, variables, statistics, denominator, formats, args, code, parent, post, …

Every column is described on its header cell’s comment in the workbook, and by tfl_spec_columns():

cols <- tfl_spec_columns("analysis_data")
knitr::kable(cols[!is.na(cols$column), c("column", "description")])
column description
2 data_id The data’s name, and its object’s name in the ARD program: a lower-case letter first, then letters, digits, _ or . – not a dataset’s or another data’s (_sub, _sub2 … are the program’s own).
3 label A name a person reads; blank: none.
4 from What it is made from: a dataset, or an analysis data of a row above.
5 population_id Keeps the subjects of this population; blank: no restriction here (made from an analysis data: that one’s population).
6 subjects Keeps the subjects of an analysis data above (a report’s own subjects: the safety set in phase 1 …): the numerator kept to the denominator’s subjects. Instead of population_id; blank: no restriction here.
7 where An R condition on the records (the numerator’s filter); blank: every record.
8 add Columns of the population’s data (its dataset, ADSL) – or of the data of subjects – added by the subject key, | between them; a column of the same name is replaced. Needs a population or subjects, here or above; blank: none.
9 derive New columns, NAME = R expression, | between them (transform()); a column the code lists list becomes a factor in their order; blank: none.
10 keep The columns kept, | between them (the subject key always); with derive, what transmute() does; blank: every column.
11 distinct One row for each set of values of these columns, | between them (dplyr::distinct(), the first row kept): a denominator per subject and phase; blank: every row.
12 code R that makes the data itself, when the columns cannot say it: its value is the data; the datasets (adae), the analysis set’s data (_sub: adsl_sub, adsl_sub2 for a report’s second) and the analysis data above are in reach. With it, the columns but from are left blank; blank: the columns make the data.

A new workbook starts from tfl_ard_spec_template(); it is read with tfl_read_ard_spec() and written with tfl_write_ard_spec(). The examples below build the sheets in R with tfl_ard_spec(), which checks them exactly as the reader does.

Datasets and populations 

base <- list(
  study = df(key = c("id", "output"),
             value = c("USUBJID", "output/ard/ard.rds")),
  datasets = df(dataset = c("ADSL", "ADAE"),
                path = c("data/adsl.rds", "data/adae.rds")),
  populations = df(population_id = "SAF", dataset = "ADSL",
                   where = 'SAFFL == "Y"'))

A population is an analysis set: the subjects of dataset for which where holds. In the program it is pop_<population_id>. An analysis row may name a dataset and a population_id: its data are then that dataset’s records of the analysis set’s subjects.

spec <- tfl_ard_spec(c(base, list(analyses = df(
  output_id = "T-14-1-1", analysis_id = "AGE", method = "continuous",
  population_id = "SAF", by = "TRT01A", variables = "AGE"))))
cat(tfl_ard_code(spec, part = "body"), sep = "\n")
report_id <- "T-14-1-1"

# ---- data ----
adsl <- readRDS("data/adsl.rds")

# ---- populations ----
# adsl_sub: SAF (SAFFL == "Y")
adsl_sub <- filter(adsl, SAFFL == "Y")

# ---- analyses ----
# AGE
ard_age <- adsl_sub |>
  ard_summary(
    by = TRT01A,
    variables = AGE,
    fmt_fun = everything() ~ fmt_default
  ) |>
  apply_fmt_fun() |>
  tag_ard(report_id, "AGE", population = "SAF")

# the report's rows of the study ARD, with the fingerprint of its
# definition (tfl_ard_spec_hash())
ard_age |>
  save_ard(report_id, definition = "3a67c8569ba5a342d3c3f784a15c74a1")

Analysis data

When several analyses read the same data – treatment-emergent events of the safety set, say – the sheet analysis_data names it once.

An analysis data is a report’s: output_id says whose, and it is required. A row’s from and subjects name only its own report’s rows above it, and an analysis reads only its own report’s data. So the same data_id may mean something else in another report – the safety set of a Phase I table and of a Phase II one – and a data two reports use is copied into each (tflplanner’s “copy from another report”).

Each row makes one data, in this order:

  1. from a dataset or an analysis data above it;
  2. kept to the subjects of a population (population_id) or of an analysis data above (subjects: the numerator kept to the denominator’s subjects);
  3. the records where keeps;
  4. columns of the population’s data added by the subject key (add);
  5. columns derived (derive), and the columns kept (keep; with derive, a transmute());
  6. one row per set of values (distinct).

data_id is the object’s name in the program. An analysis names it in its data column instead of dataset / population_id.

adata <- df(
  output_id = "T-14-3-1",
  data_id = c("adsl_saf", "adae_teae", "adae_ser"),
  label = c("Safety set", "TEAEs of the safety set", "Serious TEAEs"),
  from = c("ADSL", "ADAE", "adae_teae"),
  population_id = c("SAF", NA, NA),
  subjects = c(NA, "adsl_saf", NA),
  where = c(NA, 'TRTEMFL == "Y"', 'AESER == "Y"'),
  keep = c(NA, "AEBODSYS | AEDECOD | AESER | TRT01A", NA))

analyses <- df(
  output_id = "T-14-3-1",
  analysis_id = c("TEAE", "SER"),
  method = "hierarchical",
  data = c("adae_teae", "adae_ser"),
  by = "TRT01A",
  variables = c("AEBODSYS | AEDECOD", "AEDECOD"),
  denominator = "adsl_saf")

spec <- tfl_ard_spec(c(base, list(analysis_data = adata, analyses = analyses)))
cat(tfl_ard_code(spec, part = "body"), sep = "\n")
report_id <- "T-14-3-1"

# ---- data ----
adsl <- readRDS("data/adsl.rds")
adae <- readRDS("data/adae.rds")

# ---- analysis data ----
# adsl_saf: Safety set
adsl_saf <- filter(adsl, SAFFL == "Y")
# adae_teae: TEAEs of the safety set
adae_teae <- adae |>
  select(-any_of("TRT01A")) |>
  inner_join(select(adsl_saf, USUBJID, TRT01A), by = "USUBJID") |>
  filter(TRTEMFL == "Y") |>
  select(USUBJID, AEBODSYS, AEDECOD, AESER, TRT01A)
# adae_ser: Serious TEAEs
adae_ser <- filter(adae_teae, AESER == "Y")

# ---- analyses ----
# TEAE
ard_teae <- adae_teae |>
  ard_hierarchical_or_none(
    by = TRT01A,
    variables = c(AEBODSYS, AEDECOD),
    denominator = adsl_saf,
    id = USUBJID
  ) |>
  fmt_ard(fmt_default) |>
  tag_ard(report_id, "TEAE", population = "SAF")

# SER
ard_ser <- adae_ser |>
  ard_hierarchical_or_none(
    by = TRT01A,
    variables = AEDECOD,
    denominator = adsl_saf,
    id = USUBJID
  ) |>
  fmt_ard(fmt_default) |>
  tag_ard(report_id, "SER", population = "SAF")

# the report's rows of the study ARD, with the fingerprint of its
# definition (tfl_ard_spec_hash())
bind_rows(ard_teae, ard_ser) |>
  save_ard(report_id, definition = "cebab636000d2d2289c3e1238e45aec9")

What the columns cannot say: code

When the columns cannot say how a data is made, code is R whose value is the data. The datasets, the pop_* analysis sets and the analysis data above it are in reach. from stays (it says what the data is made from), and the other columns that make a data are left blank (this is checked):

adata2 <- adata[1:2, ]
adata2$output_id <- "T-14-3-2"     # its own copy of the two data
adata2 <- rbind(adata2, df(
  output_id = "T-14-3-2",
  data_id = "adae_first", label = "First TEAE of each subject and term",
  from = "adae_teae", population_id = NA, subjects = NA, where = NA,
  keep = NA))
adata2$code <- c(NA, NA, paste(
  "adae_teae <- adae_teae[order(adae_teae$USUBJID, adae_teae$AEDECOD), ]",
  "adae_teae[!duplicated(adae_teae[c(\"USUBJID\", \"AEDECOD\")]), ]",
  sep = "\n"))
spec2 <- tfl_ard_spec(c(base, list(
  analysis_data = adata2,
  analyses = df(output_id = "T-14-3-2", analysis_id = "FIRST",
                method = "categorical", data = "adae_first",
                by = "TRT01A", variables = "AEDECOD"))))
cat(tfl_ard_code(spec2, part = "body"), sep = "\n")
report_id <- "T-14-3-2"

# ---- data ----
adsl <- readRDS("data/adsl.rds")
adae <- readRDS("data/adae.rds")

# ---- analysis data ----
# adsl_saf: Safety set
adsl_saf <- filter(adsl, SAFFL == "Y")
# adae_teae: TEAEs of the safety set
adae_teae <- adae |>
  semi_join(select(adsl_saf, USUBJID), by = "USUBJID") |>
  filter(TRTEMFL == "Y") |>
  select(USUBJID, AEBODSYS, AEDECOD, AESER, TRT01A)
# adae_first: First TEAE of each subject and term
adae_first <- local({
  adae_teae <- adae_teae[order(adae_teae$USUBJID, adae_teae$AEDECOD), ]
  adae_teae[!duplicated(adae_teae[c("USUBJID", "AEDECOD")]), ]
})

# ---- analyses ----
# FIRST
ard_first <- adae_first |>
  ard_tabulate(
    by = TRT01A,
    variables = AEDECOD,
    fmt_fun = everything() ~ fmt_default
  ) |>
  apply_fmt_fun() |>
  tag_ard(report_id, "FIRST", population = "SAF")

# the report's rows of the study ARD, with the fingerprint of its
# definition (tfl_ard_spec_hash())
ard_first |>
  save_ard(report_id, definition = "5a928109371010b18d526b388d9cdf56")

The program carries it as <data_id> <- local({ ... }), in the sheet’s order. The spec keeps the code: the program is written from the spec and is never edited afterwards.

Analyses

One row is one cards / cardx call. Both ids become ARD columns, so a table takes its rows with tfl_ard_for(ard, output_id).

  • method: a keyword – tfl_ard_methods() lists them, each with a label a person reads – or any pkg::function of cards / cardx, or a function of the study’s own (study key source).
knitr::kable(tfl_ard_methods()[, c("method", "label", "call")])
method label call
continuous Summary statistics cards::ard_summary
categorical Counts and percents cards::ard_tabulate
dichotomous Count of one level cards::ard_tabulate_value
missing Missing counts cards::ard_missing
hierarchical Nested counts (e.g. SOC / PT) cards::ard_stack_hierarchical
max Worst level per subject cardx::ard_tabulate_max
subjects Subjects with a record (subjects)
total_n Number of subjects cards::ard_total_n
proportion_ci Proportion with CI cardx::ard_categorical_ci
mean_ci Mean with CI cardx::ard_continuous_ci
ttest t test cardx::ard_stats_t_test
wilcox Wilcoxon rank-sum test cardx::ard_stats_wilcox_test
chisq Chi-square test cardx::ard_stats_chisq_test
fisher Fisher’s exact test cardx::ard_stats_fisher_test
custom Custom R code (code)
  • by, strata, variables, statistics: | between several values. strata repeats the analysis within each combination present in the data (a parameter by visit).
  • denominator: what percentages are of – population, row, column, cell, another population, a dataset or an analysis data.
  • formats: mean=xx.x | p=xx.x% (the xx part says the decimals).
  • args: more arguments, as R (over_variables = TRUE). A function that takes a formula gets it here: formula = survival::Surv(AVAL, 1 - CNSR) ~ TRT01P.
  • parent and post: rows run inside cards::ard_stack() / ard_strata() / ard_pairwise(), and steps on the ARD after the call (cards::sort_ard_hierarchical()).

tfl_ard_functions() lists every installed cards / cardx ard_*() function by category, and tfl_ard_args() says in which column each argument of one goes:

a <- tfl_ard_args("cardx::ard_categorical_ci")
knitr::kable(a[, c("arg", "column", "choices")])
arg column choices
data data
variables variables
by by
method args waldcc | wald | clopper-pearson | wilson | wilsoncc | strat_wilson | strat_wilsoncc | agresti-coull | jeffreys
denominator denominator column | row | cell
conf.level args
value args
strata strata
weights args
max.iterations args

An analysis written as R: custom

What no column can say is written as R in code, with method custom. In the code data is the analysis data and population the analysis set’s subjects. tfl_ard_as_custom() writes an existing row as that code (the same ARD), as a starting point:

cat(tfl_ard_as_custom(spec, "T-14-3-1", "SER")$code, sep = "\n")
cards::ard_stack_hierarchical(
  data,
  by = TRT01A,
  variables = AEDECOD,
  denominator = adsl_saf,
  id = USUBJID
)

Code lists

A table spec’s codelists sheet (one row a value: output_id, variable, value, label, order) gives the order of a variable’s values and what each value is in the data the report’s program makes (label; blank: the value itself). A code list is a report’s: every row names its report, and a blank output_id is an error (a code list two reports use is copied into each; the same arm may print one way in one table and another way in the next).

Handed to the ARD program, a report’s code lists of the variables its analyses read (by, strata, variables, and the names in args, code and post) are written at the program’s head (cl_sex <- c(F = "Female", M = "Male")) and put on those columns before any analysis (set_levels(SEX = cl_sex)): each becomes a factor in the list’s order with the labels as its values, so the ARD holds “Female”, keeps the order and counts a value no record has (n = 0). A value the list does not have stops the program, naming the column and the value; a condition on such a column is written in its labels (SEX == "Female"). A variable the table only prints is not made a factor. A data made from another – an analysis set, an analysis data, an analysis’s own subset – is made factors again as its last step (|> .levels()): a value the list does not have counts only where the data analysed have it (a table of the safety set has no column for the screen failures’ arm).

codelists <- df(output_id = "T-14-1-1", variable = "SEX", value = c("M", "F"),
                label = c("Male", "Female"), order = 1:2)
spec3 <- tfl_ard_spec(c(base, list(analyses = df(
  output_id = "T-14-1-1", analysis_id = "SEX", method = "categorical",
  population_id = "SAF", by = "TRT01A", variables = "SEX"))))
cat(tfl_ard_code(spec3, part = "body", codelists = codelists), sep = "\n")
report_id <- "T-14-1-1"

# ---- code lists: each value in its order, as it is in the ARD ----
# (a value a list does not have stops the program: add it to the list)
cl_sex <- c(M = "Male", F = "Female")

# ---- data ----
adsl <- readRDS("data/adsl.rds")

# ---- populations ----
# adsl_sub: SAF (SAFFL == "Y")
adsl_sub <- adsl |>
  filter(SAFFL == "Y") |>
  set_levels(SEX = cl_sex)

# ---- analyses ----
# SEX
ard_sex <- adsl_sub |>
  ard_tabulate(
    by = TRT01A,
    variables = SEX,
    fmt_fun = everything() ~ fmt_default
  ) |>
  apply_fmt_fun() |>
  tag_ard(report_id, "SEX", population = "SAF")

# the report's rows of the study ARD, with the fingerprint of its
# definition (tfl_ard_spec_hash())
ard_sex |>
  save_ard(report_id, definition = "551d1e645d45f180865cffeac5fce902")

set_levels() and the other functions the program calls are not tflspec’s exports: tfl_helpers_code() gives their code, which a study keeps in a file of its own (tflplanner: programs/study_helpers.R), so the programs run without tflspec. A variable’s heading in a table is the variables sheet’s label; see The table spec.

Building the ARD

tfl_build_ard() runs the program from the study folder. The ARD carries output_id, analysis_id and population_id; tfl_ard_conditions() lists what went wrong while it was made (cards carries on when one analysis fails, leaving the message in the ARD).

ard <- tfl_build_ard(spec, dir = study, save = FALSE)
table(ard$analysis_id)
#> 
#>  SER TEAE 
#>  126  264
tfl_ard_conditions(ard)
#> [1] output_id   analysis_id variable    groups      level       message    
#> [7] statistics 
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

tfl_check_ard(ard, spec) checks an ARD made elsewhere (its shape, and what the tables read from it); tfl_write_ard() writes a copy as JSON, YAML or XPT. tfl_ard_spec_hash() is the fingerprint of an output’s definition, saved with the ARD so a screen can tell which outputs are out of date.

The whole program

tfl_ard_code(spec) is the whole file: the packages and helpers, the data, the analyses, saveRDS(). Write it to the study’s programs/ and run it there; tflspec is not needed to run it.

tfl_ard_code(spec, output_id = ) is one report’s program, the form a study runs (tflplanner writes one per report). The study’s program, with every report, is one part a report after the datasets and analysis sets: each part makes its own analysis data before its analyses, and, when a report has code lists, reads its data again with them – so one report’s analysis data and factors are never the next report’s.

writeLines(tfl_ard_code(spec), file.path(study, "programs", "ard.R"))
